title: AI and Marginal Revolutions in Wastewater Treatment - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Alex Tabarrok flags a French paper (co-authored by recent Nobelist Philippe Aghion) showing an AI aeration-control system in wastewater plants cut electricity use 5.4%, carbon emissions 6%, and energy spend 8.2% at negative abatement cost, with the AI's own power draw under 1% of the savings — his broader claim being that AI's real economic effect arrives as thousands of such mundane process improvements.

insights.claim: An AI aeration-control system deployed across French wastewater treatment plants cut plant electricity consumption by 5.4%, carbon emissions by 6%, and energy expenditures by 8.2% while improving effluent quality.
insights.so_what: A hard, causally identified number for industrial AI ROI in a commodity utility process — the template for underwriting AI retrofits in asset-heavy operations.
insights.quote: We find that full-time AI control reduces plants’ electricity consumption and carbon emissions by 5.4% and 6% respectively, and energy expenditures by 8.2%, resulting in negative abatement costs, while also improving water effluent quality.
insights.locator: This paper studies the environmental effects
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

insights.claim: The abatement costs of this AI deployment are negative — carbon is removed while the operator saves money — meaning adoption does not depend on carbon pricing or subsidy.
insights.so_what: Negative-cost abatement diffuses on pure economics; screen for it rather than for policy-dependent green capex.
insights.locator: This paper studies the environmental effects
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

insights.claim: The electricity the AI models themselves consume amounts to less than 1% of the electricity they save, making the model's own energy draw a rounding error at the plant level.
insights.so_what: Directly undercuts the 'AI energy hog' framing at the application layer, even if datacenter-level demand is a separate question.
insights.quote: The additional electricity demand generated by AI models represents less than 1% of these savings.
insights.locator: This paper studies the environmental effects
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

insights.claim: The post warns explicitly against reading the 'less than 1%' figure as a percentage-point offset against the 5.4/6/8.2% savings, since the two are not in the same units.
insights.so_what: A unit-mismatch trap that recurs in efficiency and emissions marketing; check denominators before netting headline percentages.
insights.quote: Don’t misread the “less than 1%” line as being in the same units as the 5.4%, 6%, and 8.2% figures above it
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

insights.claim: AI-equipped plants held up better under operational stress from extreme weather events and chemical pollutant peaks, so the value of the system includes tail-risk resilience, not just average-case efficiency.
insights.so_what: Resilience under stress is the harder-to-replicate part of the value case for industrial control AI, and it strengthens with climate volatility.
insights.quote: AI-equipped plants prove more resilient to high operational stress during extreme meteorological events and chemical pollutant peaks.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

insights.claim: The AI control system shifts plant electricity consumption from peak to off-peak hours, making industrial AI a source of demand-side flexibility rather than only a load.
insights.so_what: Watch process-AI vendors as an indirect play on grid flexibility and peak-shaving value, adjacent to storage and demand response.
insights.quote: They also improve load management by reallocating electricity consumption from peak to off-peak hours.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

insights.claim: Feeding the plant-level results into the DICE model across three diffusion scenarios yields substantial global welfare gains from the CO2 reductions of this single industrial AI use case.
insights.so_what: Scaling assumptions do the heavy lifting here — treat the aggregate welfare number as scenario output, not measurement.
insights.quote: We find substantial global welfare gains from the CO2 reductions associated with this industrial AI use case.
insights.locator: Finally, we use the DICE model
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

themes.theme: How AI actually shows up in output

insights.claim: Tabarrok's general model is that AI's economic impact will arrive through an enormous number of small, unglamorous process improvements like aeration control rather than through a few visible breakthroughs.
insights.so_what: Implies diffuse, hard-to-attribute AI gains showing up in incumbent operators' margins and utility costs rather than concentrated in AI-labeled names.
insights.quote: More generally, the effect of AI will be through many, many improvements of this nature.
insights.locator: More generally, the effect of AI
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

insights.claim: Tabarrok objects to the paper being framed as a rebuttal to AI energy-use worries, arguing those objections are innumerate and pretextual and that engaging them grants unearned credibility.
insights.so_what: Signals that AI-energy criticism functions as a proxy for other political objections — anticipate that on regulation and permitting fights.
insights.quote: But those objections are almost entirely innumerate and pretextual and casting the paper as a rebuttal lends them more credibility than they deserve.
insights.locator: One annoyance: The authors frame the paper
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok

insights.claim: The study's identification comes from quasi-experimental variation in both adoption timing and system outages across plants operated by one global water-services leader, giving unusually clean causal leverage for an industrial AI estimate.
insights.so_what: Outage-based identification is a replicable evaluation design for measuring AI value inside any always-on operational system.
insights.quote: Exploiting quasi-experimental variation in both the timing of adoption and outages, we estimate the causal impact of AI on electricity use, carbon emissions, and energy expenditures.
insights.locator: This paper studies the environmental effects
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
